subject: Biotechnology
title: In Vivo vs Ex Vivo Therapy
description: A fast breakdown of In Vivo vs Ex Vivo Therapy for builders.

hook.text: Gene therapy can happen inside the body or outside it — the choice shapes the entire treatment strategy.

buildup.text: In vivo therapy delivers vectors directly to the patient — injection into the eye, liver, or bloodstream.

discovery.text: Ex vivo therapy removes cells, edits them in the lab, and returns them — more control but more complex.

twist.text: Ex vivo works best for blood disorders — but solid organs like the brain are nearly impossible to treat this way.

climax.text: In vivo lipid nanoparticle delivery is expanding access — no cell extraction needed, just an infusion.

punchline.text: Edit outside or edit inside — each path suits different diseases.

quiz.question: When is ex vivo gene therapy preferred over in vivo?
options: When treating diseases in organs that cannot be accessed by injection
When blood cells can be extracted, edited in the lab, and safely returned
When the patient cannot tolerate any surgical procedure

details.summary: In vivo gene therapy delivers genetic material directly into the patient's body, while ex vivo therapy modifies cells outside the body and returns them. Each approach has distinct advantages in targeting, safety, and scalability that determine which diseases each strategy best addresses.
details.whyItMatters: The choice between in vivo and ex vivo delivery determines the feasibility, safety, and cost of gene therapy for specific diseases.
takeaways: In vivo therapy delivers genes directly into the patient's body using vectors
Ex vivo therapy modifies extracted cells then returns them to the patient
In vivo treats tissues that cannot be removed; ex vivo enables quality control

faq.question: When is in vivo gene therapy preferred over ex vivo?
faq.answer: In vivo therapy is necessary when target cells cannot be removed from the body, such as neurons, retinal cells, or liver cells. AAV vectors deliver genes directly to these tissues. It is simpler logistically since it does not require cell collection and manufacturing.

faq.question: What are the advantages of ex vivo gene therapy?
faq.answer: Ex vivo allows quality control of modified cells before returning them to the patient, verification that edits are correct, and expansion to therapeutic numbers. It avoids immune responses to viral vectors in the body. CAR-T and sickle cell gene therapy use ex vivo approaches.
